Book correction: The book asks to show that f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}, f(x) = e^{-x}, is bijective. As printed this is false: for x > 0, e^{-x} lies in (0, 1), so for example 2 \in \mathbb{R}^{+} is never an output (even with 0 included in \mathbb{R}^{+} the range is only (0, 1]). The intended statement is f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}, which is bijective (equally true: f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to (0, 1)).
